msg: Hello, we're a Canadian family of four visiting Cartagena over the Christmas holidays: my husband and I, plus our kids, who are 13 and 9. None of us has ever been diving. Is there something we could all do together? What are the minimum ages, and how safe is it for the children?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

What a lovely family experience—the Rosario Islands are a beautiful place to discover the reef together! Since none of you has dived before, you can choose activities that suit each person and still plan the outing together.

- *At 9:* snorkeling (from age 6) or *Bubble Makers* (ages 8–10), a shallow-water introduction with a dedicated PADI instructor, limited to a maximum depth of 2 m.
- *At 13:* snorkeling, the *Dive Mini Course* (from age 10), or an Open Water course. The mini-course includes pool practice and one ocean dive with an instructor; it does not certify you.
- *For adults:* the Dive Mini Course is the recommended first-time diving experience. Snorkeling is also an option.

The minimum age for snorkeling is 6; Bubble Makers is for ages 8–10; and the Dive Mini Course and Open Water course start at 10. Minors must be accompanied by a parent or responsible relative.

For children’s safety, Bubble Makers is conducted in a pool or very shallow water with a dedicated instructor. The mini-course includes pool practice and an instructor-led ocean dive. I can’t assess an individual child’s suitability to dive; if there’s a medical concern, please check with a team advisor.

Would you like to explore a mix of activities for your family, or have everyone snorkel together?

msg: That's really helpful, thanks. I think my husband, my 13-year-old and I would do the mini course, and our 9-year-old would do Bubble Makers. We're staying in the old town in Cartagena. How much would that come to, and could we do it on December 25th? It would make a special Christmas memory.
reply:
We only close on December 25 and January 1. The rest of the year we operate every day, including public holidays, except for suspension due to adverse weather conditions.

Guests who are not Colombian or residents of Colombia pay in US dollars (USD) by card on the website; the rate is the same, only the currency changes.

msg: Oh, that's a pity, but understandable. December 26th then. You didn't mention the price though: how much is it for the three of us doing the mini course and for our 9-year-old doing Bubble Makers?

The mini-course includes pool practice and one ocean dive with a PADI instructor; Bubble Makers is in a pool or very shallow water (maximum 2 m) with a dedicated PADI instructor. The Bubble Makers schedule and transfer details are arranged by the team.

I’m sharing the plan details below.

msg: Thanks. Two questions before we book. We fly back to Toronto on December 27th at 8 in the morning, is that okay after the dive on the 26th? And while the three of us are in the water, who is looking after our 9-year-old? Would we all be on the same boat and at the same place?
reply:
Yes—the December 27 flight at 8:00 a.m. is more than 12 hours after the Dive Mini Course’s ocean dive, which ends around noon on December 26. The 12-hour wait applies to the mini-course for non-certified divers and is counted from the last dive, not from your return to Cartagena.

Your 9-year-old would be with a dedicated PADI instructor during Bubble Makers, in a pool or very shallow water (maximum 2 m). The activities can be combined in one outing. Whether everyone travels on the same boat depends on the group size; if the group is split by activity, the team can confirm the arrangements. Would you like me to connect you with a team advisor to confirm how the Bubble Makers schedule and transfer will work for December 26?

msg: Yes, please connect me with an advisor. Should we book the mini course on the link now, or wait and sort out everything together with the advisor?
